# xurrent API reference

Python SDK for the [Xurrent REST API](https://developer.xurrent.com/v1/). Source and usage examples: [README](https://github.com/fasteiner/xurrent-python#readme).

## Getting started

Every call goes through a [XurrentApiHelper](XurrentApiHelper.md): it authenticates (API token or OAuth client credentials), follows the pagination of the API and retries on HTTP 429.

```python
from xurrent import XurrentApiHelper, Request, PredefinedFilter

x_api_helper = XurrentApiHelper("https://api.xurrent.com/v1", "<api token>", "<account>")
open_requests = Request.get_requests(x_api_helper, PredefinedFilter.open, max_results=10)
request = Request.get_by_id(x_api_helper, open_requests[0].id)
notes = request.get_notes(sort="-created_at", max_results=1)
```

## Conventions

- `Class.get_by_id(connection, id)` reads one record, `Class.get_<records>(connection, predefinedFilter, queryfilter)` lists records; `max_results` (where available) stops after that many.
- Predefined filters are enums (e.g. `PredefinedFilter.open` for `/requests/open`); `queryfilter` is a dict of field filters (`{"subject": "Printer"}`).
- Records are Python objects: the constructor arguments listed on each page plus every other field of the API response as attributes. References to other records (e.g. `request.requested_by`) become instances of their class where the page says so.
- Enum fields hold enum members for known values; a value the SDK does not know yet stays a plain string, so new values in the API do not break loading.
- Write methods (`create`, `update`, `archive`, ...) send the change to the API and return the updated record.
